source_quotes.n_subjects: We trained two adult rhesus monkeys (Macaca mulatta; monkey A: 13 kg and monkey B: 7 kg, both male) in a choice task used commonly to quantify effects of neuromodulation or neurointervention (27–31, 47–49).
source_quotes.anaesthesia: Using nonanesthetized primates performing a choice task, we found that transcranial ultrasound can have substantial and region-specific effects on target circuits.
source_quotes.adverse_events: The effect was attained using stimuli with specifications that fall within the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on diagnostic ultrasound (see Materials and Methods) (34, 35). No adverse short- or long-term effects were observed.
source_quotes.safety_notes: The effect was attained using stimuli with specifications that fall within the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on diagnostic ultrasound (see Materials and Methods) (34, 35). No adverse short- or long-term effects were observed.

flags.reason: Sessions are reported per exposure/hemisphere (e.g., 8 per monkey for left FEF, 8 for right FEF, 11 sessions of left and 11 of right motor cortex pooled across animals); the paper does not state a single combined sessions-per-subject figure.

This range is the authors' own estimate obtained by applying skull-attenuation percentages from two other papers (24% and 46/23%) to their free-field pressure, not a derating/simulation/measurement performed on the animals in this study; reported_as could not be classified into the given vocabulary and was left not_reported.
Same as exposures[0]: derived from literature attenuation estimates, not a study-specific derating.

Ultrasound was delivered 100 ms before target onset for a 300 ms duration, overlapping the early part of the choice/saccade process; the paper does not explicitly label the behavioral readout as online vs offline.

The paper discusses the auditory-confound concern and addresses it via an active-control-site (motor cortex) design rather than a specific auditory-masking method, so no auditory_control vocabulary term applies.

readout_other: two-alternative saccadic choice task with psychometric (sigmoid) curve fitting
direction_notes: Stimulation of left/right FEF biased choices toward the contralateral target (~2:1, up to ~4:1 for initial trials in a block), interpreted as a positive (excitatory) bias of the decision process represented by neurons in the stimulated region; stimulation of a control site (motor cortex) produced no significant choice bias.
safety_notes: No adverse short- or long-term effects were observed.

exposures.label: FEF stimulation (left or right frontal eye fields)

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound was applied in blocks of three to six trials, strictly interleaved with blocks of three to six trials without stimulation. The stimulus was applied for 300 ms starting 100 ms before the onset of the first target, to modulate neurons throughout the decision-making process.

exposures.label: Motor cortex control stimulation (left or right, 10 mm posterior to FEF)

timing.protocol_description: To control for indirect auditory/attentional confounds, the same stimuli were applied to a control region 10 mm more posterior to FEF (motor cortex); besides the change in stimulation location, data were collected in the same way as with FEF stimulation.
